label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Sharing my experience with Sunbelt Charter Coaches from Thursday, November 5, so other planners can factor it into their CES transportation decisions.

We booked four coaches for a 220-person client dinner at a ranch venue in Henderson, with hotel pickup scheduled for 6:15 p.m. The booking was confirmed in writing twice, most recently on Tuesday, November 3. We paid $8,400 in full: a 50% deposit in September and the balance seven days before the event.

Only two of the four coaches showed up. The first arrived 55 minutes late. That driver told me he had received the assignment at 5 p.m. The second coach broke down on the 215 with no working AC, leaving guests on the shoulder for approximately 40 minutes.

With no backup transportation provided, I put 60 guests into Ubers and Lyfts on my company card at a cost of approximately $1,900. Dinner started at 8:40 p.m. instead of 7 p.m., and the caterer charged overtime.

One late bus is something I could work through. Two missing coaches, a breakdown, and no backup plan or adequate communication are a different situation.

Sunbelt had handled two small airport runs for us well last spring, which is why I trusted them with this booking. This experience was nowhere close to that standard. My client is now reviewing whether to retain us for their March event. I can’t say how that decision will land, but the transportation failures had consequences well beyond a late dinner.

I’m requesting a refund for the two coaches that never arrived, plus reimbursement for the rideshare costs. As of this post, that remains unresolved, and calls to the office line have gone to voicemail since Friday.

Based on this experience, I would not book Sunbelt for a large event unless they can demonstrate that their dispatch, backup coverage, and event-day communication have been fixed. I’ll update this post if they respond and resolve the reimbursement request.
